images.seen: A vineyard wedding at dusk — couple posing, photographer kneeling, mother-of-the-bride in a hat looking up at a pink-grey broken sky, Cape Dutch manor behind. Saturday.
lines: One person at this wedding is checking the sky, and she has been right before.
The clouds came dressed in pink for the occasion and are behaving so far.
That sky will hold for the photographs — after that, no promises.

images.seen: A crescent moon fighting through heavy broken cloud over a dark Karoo plain, one low koppie on the horizon. Monday.
lines: The moon is down to one small window and it is using all of it.
The clouds are winning tonight, about nine rounds to one.
A sky like that keeps the heat in — the frost can stand down tonight.

images.seen: A Bengal cat curled asleep on a couch against a knitted blanket, lamp lit, heavy dark cloud over distant city lights through the window. Wednesday.
lines: Cloud right down to the rooftops, and every sensible mammal is indoors under a lamp.
Nothing is falling and nothing is shining; it is that kind of night.
A sky with no stars is the sky's way of saying go to bed.

images.seen: A white bakkie with headlights blazing on a dead-straight Karoo road at night, one bare thorn tree beside it, a completely starless overcast sky. Friday.
lines: No moon, no stars, no streetlights: tonight the headlights are the whole sky.
The sky has switched itself off for the night; the bakkie disagrees.
Overcast this thick turns the Karoo into a corridor, and he is halfway down it.
